items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the public authorities law, in relation to requiring the Long Island Power Authority to provide public notice for the construction of utility transmission facilities
items.lawCode: Ren §§1020-ii - 1020-kk to be §§1020-jj - 1020-ll, add §1020-ii, Pub Auth L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S6861

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the public authorities law, in
relation to requiring the Long Island Power Authority to provide
public notice for the construction of utility transmission facilities

 PURPOSE :

To require Long Island Power Authority (LIPA) to provide public notice
for the construction of utility transmission facilities.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1. Amends the public authorities law to require LIPA to
provide public notice before the approving any utility transmission
facilities.

Section 2. Immediate effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

Recent electric transmission projects have been initiated on Long
Island where the Long Island Power Authority (LIPA) and Public Service
Electric and Gas Company of Long Island (PSEGLI), have failed to
provide adequate public notice or consultation. The lack of public
notice and involvement has caused great controversy. These projects
have been undertaken in rural, historical and residential
neighborhoods creating adverse environmental impacts to visual
resources and community character. The spirit of the State
Environmental Quality Review Act (SEQRA) has been violated.

In projects constructed in both East Hampton and Eastport, the lack of
public notice and involvement has resulted in citizen litigation
against the utilities which is costly to ratepayers and avoidable if
the public had been involved before construction was initiated. In
East Hampton, the project had to be subsequently modified to address
community concerns.

This legislation amends the Public Authorities Law to remedy these
situations by requiring LIPA to provide public notice prior to the
construction of utility transmission facilities in the LIPA service
area that have a design capacity of 100 kV2 or less that are not
subject to the jurisdiction of Article VII of the Public Service Law.
Transmission lines which are an in-kind replacement or located
underground also are not affected by this legislation.

The bill sets forth a procedure and requirements to be followed
relating to public notice of the proposed construction of a utility
transmission facility. Such notice shall be provided by LIPA before
the environmental significance of such action is determined, pursuant
to Article VIII of the Environmental Conservation Law. The public
notice shall be provided by certified mail return receipt requested
to: (a) each municipality in which any portion of such facility is to
be located, both as primarily proposed and in the alternative
locations listed; b) each member of the legislature through whose
district the facility or any alternate would pass; and c) each
landowner who is the holder of any right, title or interest in real
property as identified from the most recent tax roll of the
appropriate municipality located within 500 feet of a proposed utility
transmission facility.

Enactment of this legislation is necessary to provide stakeholders
having an interest in a particular project with the opportunity to
participate in the review process. This would ensure that LIPA is
aware of any community and environmental concerns when considering the

approval of an application for the construction of a utility
transmission facility.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None to the State.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediately.

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 22 Chapter 520
 
       MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 6861-A, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT to amend the public authorities law, in relation to requir-
        ing the Long Island Power Authority to provide public notice for
        the construction of utility transmission facilities"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This bill would amend the Public Authorities Law to require  the  Long
Island  Power  Authority  (LIPA) to provide public notification prior to
the construction of new transmission facilities. Specifically, the  bill
would  require notification to each municipality, customer and member of
the Legislature that would be affected by a proposed transmission facil-
ity and to make documentation of the potential environmental impacts  of
the project available to the public for inspection.
 
  I  fully  support the legislative objective of requiring public notice
for future transmission projects, so that affected members of the public
and the Legislature have the opportunity to  engage  in  the  review  of
future  LIPA projects. Meaningful public involvement can only occur when
the public is  provided  with  adequate  information  about  a  proposed
project,  such as the project's location, a description of the potential
environmental impacts and an explanation of why a preferred location was
chosen. Once enacted, this bill will provide the outreach  necessary  to
allow for purposeful public engagement.
 
  While  I agree with the objectives of this bill, there are a number of
technical amendments needed to ensure that public notice occurs  in  the
most  efficient  way possible. To that end, the Executive has secured an
agreement with the Legislature  to  pass  legislation  in  the  upcoming
session  to  make  certain  alterations to the bill.  These changes will
clarify the scope of affected projects and correct  certain  references,
but  otherwise  preserve  the  laudable  goal  of providing prior public
notice of specified LIPA transmission facilities.  On that basis,  I  am
signing this bill.
 
  This bill is approved.                      (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
 
                                ______
